messages:
maria: Heads up — after the GPU fleet autoscaler kicked in in us-west-edge we started seeing internal svc DNS resolution failures for several headless services. pods can ping the node IP but DNS returns old pod IPs for a minute or two :thinking:

alex: Which services? example names and affected pods? any pattern (gpu vs cpu, node labels)?

maria: Mostly inference-* headless svcs and a few statefulset-backed services. Happens after scale-up bursts (adding 40 GPUs). Symptoms: apps get connection refused because resolver still returns IPs of pods that were evicted/terminated. kube-proxy conntrack shows entries to gone endpoints.

jon: Possible endpointSlice controller lag or kube-controller-manager API watch backlog. Can you paste `kubectl get endpointslice -n infra -l app=inference -o wide` from the time it happens? Also get `kubectl get endpoints -n infra svcname` for one affected svc.

maria: pasted output (trimmed):
```
# endpointslice for inference-a-0001 (shows 3 endpoints but pods are gone)
NAME                         ADDRESSTYPE   PORTS   ENDPOINTS
zone-inference-a-0001        IPv4          8080    10.2.4.5,10.2.4.6,10.2.4.7

# kubectl get endpoints inference-a -n infra
NAME           ENDPOINTS           AGE
inference-a     10.2.4.5:8080       2m
```

alex: Hmm. Controller seems to still list old endpoints. Any kube-controller-manager, endpointslice-controller logs?

infra-bot: autoscaler/event: scaleUp group=gpu-pool-us-west reason=scheduled_burst count=40 timestamp=2026-03-18T14:07:12Z

jon: Also check kube-proxy logs on nodes where pods moved from. We had a bug where kube-proxy conntrack didn't expire entries quickly after massive pod churn, leading to IP stickiness with headless svcs.

kevin: This is focused on headless svcs without ClusterIP? We saw similar in east last month but it was tied to kube-proxy ipvs mode + iptables hybrid. What mode are we running?

maria: We're on iptables mode for these nodes (managed edge image).

jon: Workaround that helped us before: delete the stale endpointslice(s) for the service so controller recreates them, or bounce kube-proxy on the node(s) with stale conntrack entries. Deleting endpointslices triggers resync quickly.

maria: I deleted the offending endpointslice for inference-a in the affected AZ and the service started resolving to new pod IPs within ~20s. Verified traffic recovered.

kevin: Good. For a long-term fix we should: 1) investigate controller watch latency (APIServer audit/etcd pressure), 2) tune endpointSlice GC/refresh and 3) add a targeted kube-proxy restart job post-scale-up.

alex: Can we scope whether this only affects headless? If so we can prioritize a patch for endpoint resolution path. Also add a smoke test after autoscale that queries headless svcs across AZs.

sre-ops: @oncall FYI — planning to push a canary: restart kube-proxy on 10% of nodes in the us-west-edge GPU pool after next automated scale event. Will monitor CoreDNS and endpointslice delta metrics.

maria: Rolling that canary now in staging. Will report back if it consistently prevents the stale-dns windows. Thanks all :thumbsup:
